observations.observation: The DIGITIMES report was publicly timestamped at 03:21Z on October 2, 21 minutes before cutoff. The supplied captured excerpt was collected at 03:40:26Z, 1 minute 50 seconds before cutoff.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The accessible live article is paywalled and no revision history was available. The verified pre-cutoff material is the supplied captured excerpt, not the full article.

observations.observation: The report gives a forward-looking Rubin Ultra-class power range for 2027 and an Intel Foundry-attributed 1kW-to-5kW PDN loss scenario. It presents these as industry and package-level information, not as a Micron-specific product or operating result.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: The Rubin Ultra figure is a future expectation, not a measurement of a shipped product. The accessible source does not expose the underlying Intel calculation or its assumptions, and no independent report reproducing the numerical estimate was located.

observations.observation: Before the DIGITIMES article, Intel had publicly described die-level backside-power benefits in Intel 18A designs, including reduced routing congestion and voltage droop. This supports the general technical mechanism but does not verify the article’s package-level loss scenario.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: These are company-reported results for specific Intel designs and processes, not independent verification or a general estimate for accelerator-package power delivery.

observations.observation: TrendForce’s pre-cutoff view was that CoWoS-L would remain the mainstream AI-chip packaging technology through 2028 despite EMIB-T competition, which limits any inference that packaging adoption was already shifting broadly.
observations.counterpoint_or_limit: TrendForce addresses package integration technologies, not backside power architecture, so it does not directly confirm or contradict the reported PDN-loss calculation.

gaps: No accessible original Intel Foundry slide, paper, or calculation supporting the 89W-to-2,222W loss estimate was located.
No independent contemporaneous report located within the search limit replicated the specific package-power or I²R-loss figures.
The source does not specify the assumptions behind the Rubin Ultra-class 3,500–4,000W projection or establish that it was a measured, finalized product specification.
No Micron-specific adoption, design, customer, or financial consequence is established by the material reviewed.
